changes_made.explanation: The paper is primarily about NLI classification, not NLG evaluation. While some text generation occurs as a byproduct of the generative classifier, the main focus is on classification accuracy, not evaluating or improving generated text quality. The generation is used for analysis/interpretation, not as the primary task.
No automatic metrics are used to evaluate generated text quality. The paper only uses classification metrics (accuracy, MCC) to evaluate the NLI classification performance.
No LLMs are used as judges for evaluating generated outputs.
No human evaluation of generated text is conducted. The paper only presents example generations for qualitative analysis.

overall_notes: This paper is fundamentally about natural language inference (NLI) classification, not NLG evaluation. The generative aspect is used as a means to build a better classifier, not to study or improve text generation. The text generation is a side effect of the generative modeling approach, but the evaluation focuses entirely on classification performance (accuracy, MCC) across various challenging conditions like small data, label noise, and class imbalance.
